phase: 1 - grooming and training end-to-end, driven in a real browser with demo data
title: The public landing page's grooming flow is not the governed customer journey, and cannot complete a booking on any real host
method: Drove app/page.tsx (the site root) in Chromium as a brand-new ANONYMOUS context - no session cookie at all - and again with the signed-in demo customer's session.
measured: The header reads 'Login' even when a valid customer session cookie is present: the page never reads the session. `grep -c` for every customer-session import in app/page.tsx returns 0.

Pressing 'Confirm booking' opens a modal, 'Confirm your mobile number', carrying the line 'Prototype note: OTP verification is simulated for review.' Pressing Continue issued ZERO network requests - the note is literally true, nothing is verified.
The 'Select 1 registered pet' list is a hardcoded module-level fixture, app/page.tsx:29-36 (bruno, milo, max, rio, coco, luna, simba) - not the customer's pets.
On confirm, the requests carried customerId:'WEB-9812345678' - an identity synthesised from the unverified phone - and petIds:['bruno'].

With a groomer roster published locally, the flow completed: booking PS-UAT-MTB2FAUM-F62A confirmed, work order WO-C308F819 to a real groomer, payment PAY-AAFE546C, and a NEW canonical pet PET-WEB981234567-31E645A314E2AD54150C minted from the fixture.

refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.what_I_first_suspected: That an anonymous visitor can create confirmed canonical bookings with no identity verification.
refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.why_that_is_wrong: The local run reached those endpoints only because localhost + NODE_ENV=development activates the development-preview actor (lib/development-preview.ts).
refuted_this_is_not_an_authentication_ho.measured_refutation: Driving the same real POST handlers with a non-preview request host returns 401 {"error":"Authentication required"} for BOTH /api/uat-scheduling and /api/canonical-bookings. The authorization control holds. This is stated plainly because the earlier reading was mine and it was wrong.

what_is_actually_wrong: The flow books a FIXTURE pet, not the customer's own. app/mobile-app/training-flow.tsx was already corrected for exactly this - tests/training-customer-wiring.test.mjs pins 'books the signed-in customer's own dogs, never a fixture identity'. The grooming landing page was never brought along.
Identity is derived as WEB-<phone> from a number the flow does not verify, so it is not the authenticated customer identity the rest of the platform uses.

Because it holds no session, on any host that is not a development preview its FIRST API call returns 401 - after the customer has entered name, phone, secondary phone, doorstep address, pet, safety notes and payment preference. A real customer on the live site cannot complete a grooming booking here and only finds out at the end.

app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx is the governed twin: it loads the customer's own pets, resolves the service location, and books through createCanonicalLifecycle. app/mobile-app/page.tsx renders it EMBEDDED. So a correct grooming journey exists; the site root runs a different, older one.
why_not_fixed_here: The remedy is a product decision, not a defect fix: route / to the governed flow, gate its CTA behind real sign-in, or make / marketing-only and send booking to /mobile-app. Each changes what the public site does. Choosing one would be inventing product semantics, which this audit does not do.
severity: Launch-blocking for the grooming journey as presented on the public site, and only for that surface. No data was exposed and no control was bypassed.
not_claimed: No production or staging system was touched. Every measurement is local.
The booking created during this probe exists only in the local .wrangler dev database.
